text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 are not observed at all; in the later window each occurs in a substantial share of traces — about 37 in 100 for A19, 29 for A20 and 34 for A25 — at roughly 36% of the trace's event positions. [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- In the later window, each of the three leads almost exclusively to A26: about 96 in 100 of A19's observed outgoing transitions go to A26, about 98 of A20's and 97 of A25's; earlier, these activities had no observed outgoing transitions. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- The three behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: A19 and A20 never share a trace and A20 and A25 never do (earlier because both were absent, later because only one of them runs), A19 and A25 share about 1 in 200 traces, and together the three cover essentially every later trace. [REL001, REL002, REL007]
- A41's outgoing behaviour changed completely: earlier, about 93 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went directly to A26; later, about 34 in 100 go to A19, 31 to A25 and 27 to A20, with only about 1 in 100 still going directly to A26. [DIR004]
- The ordering is consistent with a chain: A41 precedes A19, A20 and A25 (in about 37, 28 and 33 of 100 traces respectively), and each of the three precedes A26 (in 37, 28.5 and 34 of 100) and the later A31; earlier, A41 and A26 co-occurred in every trace with A41 first. [REL006, REL010, REL014, REL003, REL008, REL011, REL004, REL009, REL012]
- Consequently the direct A41→A26 succession became indirect: the distance from A41 to A26 was one event in about 94 of 100 cases earlier and is two events in about 90 of 100 cases later; A26 still occurs in every trace, with its mean position shifting slightly later (about 0.37 to 0.39 of the trace). [LAG002, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that in the later window a per-case choice among three activities — A19, A20 or A25 — is inserted between A41 and A26: A41, which previously led almost directly to A26, now leads to exactly one of the three (about 34, 31 and 27 in 100 of its transitions), and the chosen activity leads on to A26 (about 96–98 in 100). The signs are direct and mutually consistent: the three activities are absent from the earlier window and present in 28–37 of 100 traces later; they are mutually exclusive and together cover essentially all traces; relational items show A41 before each of the three and each of the three before A26; and the A41→A26 distance moved from one event to two. The 25 qualifying control-flow items far exceed the roughly 0.35 expected without change, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. Limitations: many items describe the same insertion and are not independent confirmations; the evidence cannot show what determines which of the three alternatives runs in a given case, and it cannot fully rule out that these activities already existed but were not executed in the earlier sample. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL003, REL006, REL008, REL010, REL011, REL014, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003]

Other differences: A31 occurs in all traces in both windows but sits slightly later in the later window (mean position about 0.69 vs 0.71), consistent with the extra event inserted before it [POS005]; the gap between A31 and A35 shifted from mostly one event (about 55 in 100 cases) to mostly two events (about 62 in 100), a modest redistribution the main hypothesis does not cover [LAG001].
